subject.title: Feature Request: Voice Recognition / Speaker Identification for Voice Interface

question: Should OpenClaw add enrolled-speaker verification to native voice input, and what storage, provider-egress, fallback, and platform-scope contract should govern it?
rationale: The request is valid and security-aligned, but the permanent boundary cannot be inferred from current code because it affects biometric-like state, probabilistic authorization, provider routing, and multiple native voice surfaces.

options.title: Design speaker-gate contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require maintainer-approved enrollment, storage, provider-egress, fallback, and platform-scope design before any implementation PR.

options.title: Defer to ASR/provider work
options.body: Treat this as blocked on the custom ASR/native audio provider decisions and revisit speaker identity only after those seams exist.

options.title: Decline as an auth boundary
options.body: Decide that speaker recognition should not gate OpenClaw commands because voice matching is too probabilistic for the intended security model.

recommendation.title: Design speaker-gate contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require maintainer-approved enrollment, storage, provider-egress, fallback, and platform-scope design before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest sampled history across macOS voice wake, push-to-talk, Talk routing, and native-node voice surfaces.
